chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from al-Husayn al-Bazzaz, who said:

I commanded whoever asks Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Is the wealth for the close relatives or for the agnates?' He said,ates?' He said, 'The wealth is for the close relatives, and the agnates are dust in his mouth.'

key_terms.الْأَقْرَبِ: the close relatives (specifically those with direct ties)
key_terms.الْعَصَبَةِ: the agnates (male relatives who inherit by virtue of being male and related through the male line)
key_terms.فِي فِيهِ: in his mouth (idiomatic expression for dismissal or insignificance)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits first, close relatives or agnates, according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the hierarchy of inheritance, prioritizing close relatives (al-aqrab) over agnates (al-asabah) by dismissing the latter's claim as 'dust in his mouth.' This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the proximity of kinship ties over the broader tribal lineage often emphasized in Sunni fiqh, reinforcing the Quranic principle of specific shares for primary heirs.
